data.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Global Commodity Trading
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, a major Microsoft service outage on Thursday affected government agencies, businesses and traders worldwide, forcing some trading teams to switch to phone calls, fax and instant messaging. The outage added complexity to crude oil trading amid tensions in the Middle East and delayed the release of some commodity price data.

Microsoft said recovery efforts were progressing, but more than 20 products and services could still experience errors.

data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Bitcoin infrastructure company Blockstream and Thales have partnered to launch an institutional digital asset custody solution. Adam Back said offline cold storage can reduce the risk of cyberattacks.

data.title: U.S. Treasuries Close Mixed as Yield Curve Steepens
data.description:
U.S. Treasuries closed mixed on Friday as the yield curve steepened, with short-term yields falling about 1 basis point and intermediate- to long-term yields rising 2–3 basis points. According to Sina Finance, at 4:23 p.m. New York time, the 2-year yield was down 2.2 basis points at 4.8589%, the 5-year yield was little changed at 4.9706%, the 10-year yield was up 1.4 basis points at 5.1413%, and the 30-year yield had risen 2 basis points to 5.472%.

Just after 3 p.m. New York time, the spread between 2-year and 10-year yields widened by more than 3 basis points. The 10-year yield was around 5.15%, up about 2.5 basis points on the day, after briefly rising above 5.17% for the first time since October 14. Short-term Treasuries reversed earlier losses after U.S. stocks fell, led by Nasdaq 100 constituents.

Long-end swap spreads led gains, closing near their intraday highs and widening nearly 2 basis points on Friday after expanding 1.5 basis points on Thursday. Swaps underperformed Treasuries, and demand for fixed-rate payments may have been related to convexity and contributed to higher yields. Overnight index swaps linked to Fed meeting dates closed little changed, pricing in expectations for about 28 basis points of rate hikes at the December policy meeting. The 5-year/30-year Treasury yield spread rose about 2 basis points to 49.96 basis points, the 2-year/10-year spread widened about 3.7 basis points to 28.03 basis points, and 10-year Treasury futures fell 0.2%.

data.description: U.S. stocks finished the week higher amid tech turmoil, Bloomberg reported. Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio and YouTube provided cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close with Vonnie Quinn, Bailey Lipschultz, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Weighs Bridge Loan to Help Venezuela Repay $2.3 Billion IDB Debt
data.description: According to Jin10, the U.S. Treasury is considering a short-term bridge loan to help Venezuela repay about $2.3 billion in debt owed to the Inter-American Development Bank (IDB) and restore its eligibility for financing. The IDB approved resuming engagement with Venezuela on Friday. After the debt is repaid, Venezuela could receive up to $6 billion in IDB loans over the next two years, while the World Bank could also provide up to $5 billion during the same period. The U.S. plan would provide funds to the IDB through an overnight financing arrangement rather than directly to Venezuela. The proposal could draw attention from Congress. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren previously opposed using the Exchange Stabilization Fund to guarantee financial institutions investing in Venezuela.

data.title: International Oil Prices Diverge on the 13th as Light Crude Falls and Brent Rises
data.description: According to Jin10, international oil prices were mixed on the 13th: December-delivery light crude futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange fell 18 cents to $88.56 a barrel, down 0.2%, while January-delivery Brent crude futures rose 2 cents to $95.84 a barrel, up 0.02%.

data.title: STOCKS | Harvest Fund Adds Nvidia in Third Quarter, Keeping It as Its Top Holding
data.description:
An analysis of Harvest Fund’s 13F filing found that it increased its Nvidia holdings in the third quarter, leaving the stock as its largest position and raising its portfolio weighting to 7.1%.

According to Sina Finance, Harvest Fund also added Alibaba and exited its positions in KE Holdings and GDS Holdings.

The analysis covered 463 disclosed investments with a total market value of $3.24 billion. Harvest Fund is one of China’s largest asset managers, and its website reports assets under management of more than RMB 1.8 trillion ($269.8 billion).

data.title: CFTC Chief Seeks Aluminum Pricing Reforms as Costs Rise
data.description: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission chief called for reforms to aluminum pricing, and the agency is examining how prices are set, Bloomberg reported. Aluminum reached a record in the US this year, boosting costs for domestic beverage makers that use the metal in beer and soda cans.

data.title: Joe Carlasare: Bitcoin’s Extreme Fear Is Why He Is Buying
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bitcoin Magazine, Bitcoin attorney Joe Carlasare said in a video interview that the market is in one of the worst phases he has seen, but that extreme fear is why he is buying. He noted that Bitcoin rose from $57,000 to $82,000 in less than 90 days this year, challenging the view that capital cannot flow back into the market. A move to $80,000-$90,000 could draw technical traders and momentum investors off the sidelines, he said, while a return to $100,000 could quickly change the market narrative.

Carlasare described early-holder selling that weighed on Bitcoin in 2025 as a healthy shakeout. He said rising yields reflect economic growth rather than a debt crisis and advised watching seasonal inflation and the lag in Federal Reserve policy. He also said investment outcomes are about 90% dependent on psychology, argued that Bitcoin needs a serious quantum-computing response to attract new capital, and said divided government could support markets.

data.title: Rescues Underway After Tanker Hits New Orleans River Cruise Boat on Mississippi River
data.description: According to CNBC, a tanker struck the American Heritage river cruise boat, which had 129 passengers aboard, on Friday, partially submerging it in the Mississippi River near New Orleans. The tanker was identified as Atlantic Asphalt, and the cruise boat is operated by American Cruise Lines. Authorities had not immediately said whether anyone was injured or killed. New Orleans Emergency Medical Services Lt. Stephanie C. Norwood said agencies were responding to the rescue effort.

data.title: FAA Issues Nationwide Ground Stop
data.description: According to CNBC, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, citing extraordinary circumstances. A ground stop halts departing flights at their origin.

data.title: AI Risks Are the Biggest Threat to the Financial System, Fed Survey Finds
data.description: According to CNBC, 87% of respondents to a Federal Reserve survey released Friday cited artificial intelligence as a salient risk to the financial system, up from 50% in the survey during the spring of this year. A risk asset correction was the next most-cited concern, at 52%, followed by higher long-term rates at 48%, cyberattacks at 43% and fiscal debt sustainability at 43%. Respondents pointed to elevated equity valuations, cybersecurity threats and complex AI-related financing as areas of concern. The report covered the period up to Oct. 28 and described the financial system as fairly stable, while noting that hedge fund leverage was at its highest since 2013 and concentrated among a relatively small group.

data.title: London Metal Exchange Spot Tin Surges as Falling Inventories Tighten Supply
data.description: London Metal Exchange (LME) spot tin prices surged as buyers faced supply constraints, with the metal trading at a $670-per-tonne premium to the benchmark three-month contract on Friday. According to Sina Finance, inventories supporting LME contract trading have fallen nearly 60% since June. Copper and aluminum inventories have also declined in recent months, driving large spot premiums in those markets. As short positions approach expiry, the spot-price surge could put significant pressure on holders and often trigger competition for deliverable metal.

data.title: Federal Reserve: AI Investment Cycle Could Soon Surpass 1990s Telecom Cycle
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, a Federal Reserve report says investment in artificial intelligence computing is accelerating and the current investment cycle could soon exceed the scale of the 1990s telecommunications cycle.

data.description: Nvidia said speculation that it is engaging with potential CEO candidates is premature and that it is still selecting a firm to find a successor to ousted leader Jensen Huang, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: After Mukesh Ambani, Sunil Mittal Sets Local-Control Condition for Elon Musk’s Starlink
data.description:
Bharti Airtel Chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal said Starlink can enter India only if its network’s “kill switch” and control remain in the country. Mittal told NDTV on November 13 that Elon Musk seemed impatient and frustrated, according to BeInCrypto. Mittal’s group backs OneWeb, a Starlink rival also awaiting approval, and he said Starlink’s sale in India would be “all right” with local control.

The issue drew attention after SpaceX’s Starshield, its military version of Starlink, was slowed in Ukraine from Oct. 14 to 24, United24 reported. Musk said the decision was made by U.S. President Donald Trump; Starshield is owned and controlled by the U.S. government, while Starlink is a commercial SpaceX service. Mittal said Starlink’s laser links let data bypass Indian ground stations, unlike OneWeb’s system; Tech Insider reported that the design conflicts with India’s security rules.

Jio Platforms, owned by Mukesh Ambani, listed Oct. 28 at ₹1,119 ($11.68) in India’s largest IPO and traded near ₹1,400 on Nov. 13. Jio holds 42.6% of fixed broadband lines and 77.5% of 5G home wireless, markets where Starlink could compete once approved. Musk accused Ambani of blocking Starlink; India denied bias and said Starlink filed security papers last. Mittal said in October he would welcome approval days before Musk’s and questioned demand, noting Indians can get 5G for about $3 a month—around one-tenth of satellite service’s price. India’s Cabinet must still set spectrum fees, and the Home Ministry must clear each operator before sales can begin.
